domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Rewrite operands into a compatible structural form before subtraction, including normalizing whole numbers or mixed numbers and converting fractional parts to a common denominator when needed.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory setup skills used to make subtraction possible. They occur in the same problem-solving phase before any actual subtraction is carried out. Although they are not identical operations, they are diagnostically close as operand-preparation actions and can be meaningfully combined at a coarser grain.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract whole-number parts and/or fractional parts once the quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a shared denominator.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because execution of subtraction is a distinct cognitive operation from setup, regrouping, simplification, and answer formatting. It remains a major diagnostic breakpoint.

skills.name: Regroup for subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow 1 from the whole-number part and convert it into fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract the subtrahend's fractional part.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because regrouping has a distinctive error pattern and is not always required. Students may subtract aligned parts correctly yet fail specifically at borrowing across whole and fractional parts.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms or rewrite a zero-valued fraction as 0 after subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a post-subtraction transformation with its own common errors and is not required on every item.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Combine computed whole-number and fractional parts into the final answer form, including writing the result as a mixed number, pure fraction, integer, or 0 as appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final presentation/recombination is distinct from arithmetic execution and from simplification. Students can compute correctly but still misstate the final form.
